office_does: A State Representative is one of the 29th District's two members of the Washington House, voting on state law and budgets.
race_blurb: Four-term Democratic incumbent Melanie Morgan faces Democrat Krista Perez, a first-time candidate endorsed by the 29th LD Democrats. Morgan voted against the 2026 millionaires' tax and Perez backs it.

candidates.summary: Department of Commerce partnerships manager, DEI consultant and founder of the Tacoma Women of Color Collective, running for 'new leadership' on fair taxation, workers' rights, reproductive freedom and immigrant protections.
highlights: Backs the millionaires' tax and calls for 'flipping' Washington's regressive tax system [S4]
Pledges to keep Washington a sanctuary regardless of immigration status [S4]
Would expand affordable-housing funding and tenant protections and reform the GMA for middle-density housing [S4]
Endorsed by the 29th LD Democrats, Washington State Labor Council, Fuse Washington and seven Tacoma councilmembers [S1][S5][S6]

taxes.basis: Pamphlet pledges 'fair taxation'; site backs the millionaires' tax and calls for flipping the regressive tax structure to raise revenue.

spending.basis: Would expand Working Connections Child Care, the Working Families Tax Credit and housing funding, and wants revenue to unlock those investments.

housing.basis: More state affordable-housing funding and tenant protections, alongside GMA reform for middle-density development.

safety.basis: Emphasizes youth gun-violence programs and wraparound treatment services for root causes; no enforcement planks.

climate.basis: Supports immediate action to reduce carbon emissions and green union jobs.

experience.basis: No elected office; running for 'new leadership' against a four-term incumbent.

immigration.basis: Pledges that Washington remain a sanctuary regardless of immigration status and lists protecting immigrant communities in the pamphlet.

social.basis: Pamphlet and site pledge to protect and expand reproductive freedom and push back on any limits to reproductive autonomy.

candidates.summary: Four-term incumbent, former Franklin Pierce school board director and Army veteran, running as 'unbought and unbossed' on housing, healthcare, public safety and equity.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346 (2026 millionaires' tax), unlike seatmate Rep. Sharlett Mena [S4]
Voted for the 2021 capital gains tax and the 2025 capital gains, services and B&O revenue bills [S7][S8][S9][S10]
Voted for EHB 1217 rent limits and E2SHB 1110 middle housing [S11][S12]
Led creation of the $200 million Community Reinvestment Account and the CROWN Act [S3]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 2021 capital gains tax and the 2025 revenue bills, but against ESSB 6346, the 2026 income tax on millionaires.

spending.basis: Cites appropriations for the district and led the $200 million Community Reinvestment Account.

housing.basis: Voted for EHB 1217 rent limits and E2SHB 1110 zoning reform, and cites both in her statement.

safety.basis: Voted against Initiative 2113 on police pursuits; the Community Reinvestment Account funds violence prevention and reentry.

experience.basis: Four-term incumbent with caucus leadership roles and school-board service, against a first-time candidate.

local-control.basis: Voted for E2SHB 1110, the state mandate requiring cities to allow middle housing.

social.basis: Voted for ESSB 5599 on youth access to protected health care; no further statements found.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296's amendments to the I-2081 parental-rights list; no statement found.
